items.title: Rust is entering CPython carefully
items.oneliner: CPython targets optional Rust support in 3.16. Python is finally trading C legacy for memory safety.

items.title: A 125B model hits consumer GPUs
items.oneliner: Qwen 3.8 Flash Next reportedly runs on an RTX 4090 at 100 tok/s. Local inference just got more serious.

items.title: OpenAI culture criticism went public
items.oneliner: An OpenAI resignation turned safety concerns into mainstream scrutiny. Governance is now a product risk, not PR.

items.title: Git hooks became a credential trap
items.oneliner: A fake client project hid a malicious post-checkout hook. Cloning untrusted repos now looks like opening malware.

items.title: C2PA timestamps have trust gaps
items.oneliner: C2PA timestamping can be gamed through spec quirks and self-certification. Provenance still is not proof.

items.title: Connected cars are constant data brokers
items.oneliner: Researchers found over 75% of tested cars and companion apps talk to third parties. Your vehicle is telemetry.

items.title: Rust builds got a real speedup
items.oneliner: Early metadata emission cuts cargo check by up to 54%. Rust compile times may finally bend downward.

items.title: Zig shipped a major toolchain update
items.oneliner: Zig 0.17.0 lands a rebuilt build system and incremental ELF linker work. The language is maturing below syntax.

items.title: gVisor is moving to CNCF
items.oneliner: Google is donating gVisor to CNCF. Sandbox isolation just got a better shot at neutral governance and adoption.

items.title: Usage-based AI needs hard caps
items.oneliner: Soft spend alerts are not enough for agentic systems. Default hard budget caps are becoming infrastructure hygiene.
